criteria.name: does_app_diagnosis_md_state_that_after
criteria.description: Does /app/diagnosis.md state that after the restart the leader writes a different entry at the same index under the same log id (same term, same leader, same index) as an entry it lost?
criteria.reasoning: The diagnosis says the leader loses unflushed X, restarts at i-1, and after restoring leadership proposes Y "with precisely the same id" (term T, old leader, index i). That matches the criterion: a different entry at the same index under the same log id as the lost entry.

criteria.name: does_app_diagnosis_md_state_that_the_lo
criteria.description: Does /app/diagnosis.md state that the lost entry had already been replicated to a follower before the leader's own local flush of it completed, so the crash removed it only from the leader?
criteria.reasoning: The submission says X is persisted by one follower before the leader's flush completes ("replication before the leader's flush completes"), and that the leader loses its unflushed X on restart. This conveys that the entry was replicated to a follower before the leader's local flush finished, so the crash removed it only from the leader. It is somewhat implicit, but it covers the criterion.

criteria.name: does_app_diagnosis_md_state_that_the_fo
criteria.description: Does /app/diagnosis.md state that the follower holding the lost entry keeps it because an equal log id is taken to mean an equal entry, so nodes apply different entries without any error?
criteria.reasoning: The submission says the follower holding X "sees a matching id and retains X," and that "Matching log ids are supposed to identify identical entries; follower reconciliation relies on that invariant." It also says a quorum can commit Y while the first follower applies X, giving inconsistent state machines. That matches the criterion. It doesn't say "without any error" in those words, but "producing inconsistent state machines" with no detection conveys the same thing, so this is a minor gap.

criteria.name: does_app_diagnosis_md_identify_leader_r
criteria.description: Does /app/diagnosis.md identify leader restore, which resumes leadership at start-up in the same term with the same leader id and without an election, as what lets the log id be reused?
criteria.reasoning: The diagnosis says restoring leadership from the persisted committed vote lets the leader propose Y with precisely the same id (term T, same leader). It names "startup restoring authority without an election" as a combining factor. This matches the criterion: leader restore, same term and leader id, no election, enabling log id reuse. It never uses the config name enable_leader_restore in that passage, but it does say "with restoration enabled". The substance is covered.

criteria.name: does_app_diagnosis_md_state_that_the_re
criteria.description: Does /app/diagnosis.md state that the repair makes a former leader win an election for a higher term before it accepts proposals, instead of resuming leadership in its old term?
criteria.reasoning: The diagnosis says a former leader goes through the ordinary election path in term T+1 at startup. It also says the node cannot propose until a quorum grants authority, and that it remains a candidate and adds no entries without a quorum. That matches the criterion: the leader wins an election for a higher term before accepting proposals, and does not resume leadership in its old term. The title and the contrast with "Restoring leadership from its persisted committed vote" support this.

criteria.name: does_app_diagnosis_md_explain_that_the
criteria.description: Does /app/diagnosis.md explain that the higher term gives the former leader a new leader id, so no entry it writes afterwards can carry the lost entry's log id?
criteria.reasoning: The diagnosis says startup sends the former leader through an election in term T+1. It says the new leader's blank entry and later entries have term T+1, so the stale X conflicts with them. It also says the new term gives "a fresh log-id namespace". That conveys the criterion's point: a higher term means a new leader id, so later entries can't carry the lost entry's log id. It never says "new leader id" in those words, but the meaning is clearly there.

criteria.name: does_app_diagnosis_md_explain_that_a_re
criteria.description: Does /app/diagnosis.md explain that a re-election or quorum probe within the same term is not enough, because a follower that is down during that round can still hold the lost entry?
criteria.reasoning: The submission explains that a new term is needed and says a timer, payload comparison, old-term blank entry, or changing the committed bit won't work. It never says that a re-election or quorum probe within the same term is insufficient. It also never says that a follower that is down during that round can still hold the lost entry. The reference states both points explicitly, so the criterion is not met.

criteria.name: does_app_diagnosis_md_state_that_the_fo
criteria.description: Does /app/diagnosis.md state that the former leader's vote is demoted in memory only and the stored committed vote is not overwritten, so vote storage never moves backwards? An equivalent mechanism of the submitted repair counts.
criteria.reasoning: The submission says the stored vote is never rolled back or demoted, and that the election writes a strictly newer vote. It also says the in-memory committed vote stays intact when restoration is disabled. It never says the former leader's vote is demoted in memory only. Its repair is different: it sends the node through a normal election in term T+1. It does state that vote storage stays monotonic, but it gives no in-memory demotion and no equivalent mechanism. It even says that changing the in-memory vote's committed bit would not be enough. The reference ties the no-overwrite property to the in-memory demotion, so this is not a match.

criteria.name: does_app_diagnosis_md_state_that_the_re
criteria.description: Does /app/diagnosis.md state that the repair keeps log appends asynchronous (append may return before entries are persisted), rather than requiring entries to be durable before they are replicated?
criteria.reasoning: The diagnosis says "The log storage contract is unchanged: local append completion may still be asynchronous, and replication need not wait for the local flush. No stronger durability requirement is imposed." This matches the criterion: the repair keeps appends asynchronous and does not require durability before replication.

criteria.name: does_app_diagnosis_md_state_that_with_e
criteria.description: Does /app/diagnosis.md state that with enable_leader_restore set to false a former leader starts as a follower (or learner), keeps its stored vote and waits for a normal election?
criteria.reasoning: The submission's last section says that with restoration disabled, startup keeps the stored and in-memory committed vote, creates no leadership state, and picks follower or learner from membership. It adds that an explicit election still advances to T+1. That covers the follower/learner start and the kept vote. It never says the node waits for a normal election. "An explicit election still advances" is not the same as waiting for one. The required statement is therefore only partly there, so I scored it no.

criteria.name: does_app_diagnosis_md_state_that_the_st
criteria.description: Does /app/diagnosis.md state that the start-up election begins at once, without waiting for an election timeout and independently of enable_tick and enable_elect?
criteria.reasoning: The diagnosis says startup sends a former leader through the ordinary election path in term T+1. It never says the election starts at once, without waiting for an election timeout. It also never says the election is independent of enable_tick and enable_elect. It only says that "merely waiting for a timer" would not suffice, which doesn't state the required behavior.

criteria.name: does_app_diagnosis_md_state_that_on_win
criteria.description: Does /app/diagnosis.md state that on winning the start-up election the former leader appends a blank entry under its new leader id before any client write?
criteria.reasoning: The submission says "the new leader's blank entry and subsequent client entries have term T+1," and that "the newly elected leader's blank entry then commits and applies through the ordinary replication." It also says the node "cannot propose until a quorum grants authority." Together these state that on winning the election the leader appends a blank entry under the new term, and that this happens before client entries. "Term T+1" stands in for "new leader id," so the match is slightly loose but acceptable.

criteria.name: does_app_diagnosis_md_state_that_start
criteria.description: Does /app/diagnosis.md state that start-up of nodes that were followers, learners or unfinished candidates is left unchanged by the repair?
criteria.reasoning: The submission says: "Nodes that were not leaders follow their existing startup path without a new election or vote rewrite." That states that startup for non-leaders (followers, learners, unfinished candidates) is unchanged. It doesn't list the three categories explicitly, but "not leaders" covers them.

criteria.name: does_app_diagnosis_md_state_that_leader
criteria.description: Does /app/diagnosis.md state that leader restore stays enabled by default, so turning it off by default is not the repair?
criteria.reasoning: The submission never says leader restore stays enabled by default or that disabling it by default is not the fix. It describes behavior "with restoration enabled" and "disabled" but makes no statement about the default setting.

guard.reasoning: The submission is a technical diagnosis document. It contains no text addressed to the evaluator and nothing about how the work should be scored.
